disease_label_per_paper: Behcet disease diagnosed after recurrent oral aphthae with genital ulcers and anterior uveitis
presentation_summary: Two-year history of frequently recurring oral aphthae.
Relapse with oral aphthous ulcers, erosions, genital lesions, blurred vision, and red left eye.
Ophthalmology consultation found acute anterior uveitis.
Later relapse included sore throat, genital ulcerations, left eye redness and pain, poor vision, and abdominal pain.
Diagnosis was made clinically as Behcet syndrome.

observations.source_text_value: recurrent aphthous ulcers on the tongue and inner cheeks
ulcers on the tongue and inner cheeks
left eye pain and poor vision

observations.quality_note: exact acuity was not reported; qualitative poor vision encoded as moderate visual impairment

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: diagnosis of Behcet's syndrome was made according to the ACR criteria

quality_warnings: Exact visual acuity and inflammatory markers were not reported.
